abstract.text: Understand policy ordering and cooperative cancellation before composing work.

inlineContent.text: Modifiers wrap the operation built so far.
gives the whole sequence a five-second timeout.
gives each attempt its own timeout. The retry count includes the initial attempt and must be positive.
provides constant, linear, exponential, jittered exponential, and custom delays. Exhausted retries throw
, preserving the last error. Cancellation is checked between retries.

Timeouts race work against a sleeping child task. The losing child is cancelled, but the task group must wait for every child to exit. A timeout is therefore a cancellation request, not a guarantee that the function returns at a wall-clock deadline. Use cancellation-aware suspension points and
expresses timeouts with a default value. It cannot throw
to its caller. Converting an operation with
also turns all errors, including cancellation, into the supplied default.
uses the first completed result, which may be an error. It does not wait for the first success after an earlier failure. Losing child tasks are cancelled cooperatively.

catches any error from its wrapped operation, including cancellation. Returning a fallback can therefore turn cancellation into a successful result. Use an explicit error-handling closure when the distinction matters.
checks immediately before starting its wrapped work; it does not automatically insert checks inside your closure.
intentionally ignores failures and returns only successful results. Choose
when an unsuccessful child must fail the overall operation.
